summary: The note describes a national initiative to integrate coding and computational thinking into the K-12 curriculum, announced by Minister of Education Dr. Emily Thompson on September 15, 2023. It covers the historical background, teacher training through "Code Forward", the cross-subject approach, equity efforts via "Code Equity", community engagement, and new assessment methods being developed.
one_line: A national K-12 curriculum initiative integrates coding and computational thinking, supported by teacher training, equity programs, community engagement and new assessment tools.
key_facts: On September 15, 2023, Minister of Education Dr. Emily Thompson announced that coding and computational thinking would be formally incorporated into the national K-12 curriculum starting the following academic year.
Dr. Emily Thompson said understanding the language of computers is "as fundamental as reading, writing, and arithmetic."
Jeannette Wing was a pioneer who argued in the early 2000s for computational thinking, a problem-solving methodology using concepts fundamental to computer science.
The UK took the lead by introducing a new computing curriculum in 2014, paving the way for other nations.
"Code Forward", led by tech companies such as MicroTech Solutions, provides resources and training to thousands of teachers nationwide, in collaboration with the Department of Education.
Since October 3, 2023, "Code Forward" has offered professional development sessions, online courses, and a community of practice for educators.
John Sampson, CEO of MicroTech Solutions, said "Teachers are the backbone of educational transformation."
Coding and computational thinking are woven into language arts, mathematics and the sciences rather than confined to computer science classrooms.
"Code Equity" was launched on November 20, 2023 by the government and private partners to give underserved communities technological infrastructure and educational resources.
A major challenge is equitable access, since rural or underfunded school districts risk widening the gap between the haves and have-nots.
Community engagement includes parent workshops, public coding events, and collaboration with local businesses; Luisa Gomez says community involvement is pivotal.
Assessment is moving beyond test scores to portfolios, teacher observations, project-based learning outcomes and student self-reflections.
A committee of specialists began designing new evaluative tools on December 1, 2023 and is expected to present initial findings by mid-2024.
